# Review: "Italy and the Gulf Shock: Fuel, Freight, Prices and the Risk of a Truck Strike" (November 2026)

**Reviewer:** independent review (fact-checking and editing), carried out with an AI assistant · **Date:** 10 November 2026, morning (data read 06:15–06:50 UTC)
**Text reviewed:** [`report/italy-gulf-shock-2026-11.md`](../italy-gulf-shock-2026-11.md) and [`docs/report/en/italy-gulf-shock-2026-11.html`](../../docs/report/en/italy-gulf-shock-2026-11.html), both generated by [`report/build_italy.py`](../build_italy.py)
**Standard:** [`report/STANDARD.md`](../STANDARD.md)

## Summary

- **Claims checked: 120** (every number in the text, tables and captions, and the dated facts): **88 confirmed, 25 corrected, 7 not verifiable from here** (plus four items the report lists as missing, section 6). Many numbers appear in several places (key points, body, indicators table); each is counted once.
- All corrections were made **at the source**, in `report/build_italy.py` (text blocks, the `EXTERNAL` table and one recomputation in `compute()`), then the report was regenerated. No data file was touched.
- The three most serious problems:
  1. **Brent.** The 91.70 dollars that `prezzi.json` records under 9 November is **not the 9 November close**. The file was read at 03:40 UTC on 10 November, during the overnight trading of the 10 November session (Yahoo hourly bars: 91.73 at 02:00 and 91.57 at 03:00 UTC). The final close of the 9 November session is **92.57** (Yahoo daily bar, read 06:49 UTC on 10 November, −5.85% on the day). The 92.62 used by the risk dashboard and the Hormuz report is an intraday reading at 19:47 UTC on 9 November, 5 cents from the close. The brief asked to use 91.70 as "the final close": the data show it is not, so the report now quotes 92.57 and explains all three figures. The scenarios keep the simulator's 91.70 base (it is in `italia-impatti.json`); the effect on the diesel results is under half a cent.
  2. **Key point 1** said "Diesel is back near €2.29 a litre after the last excise cut expired". That is a calculation (net price + full excise), not an observation, and the observations contradict it: the Mimit self-service average went from €2.224 on 7 November (last day of the cut) to €2.232 on 9 November, +0.8 cents against the 4.9 cents of the cut; the ministry credits the price caps. The report also compared the 2.232 self-service figure with the MASE mixed self-service/attended average without saying so.
  3. **Haulage tax credit.** The report and its Limits said Unatras reported "434 million of credits not yet reached firms". The source says firms had not yet received the credit "for which [Unatras] indicates resources allocated of 434 million". Both 434 and 480 are **allocations**; the conflict is between two allocation totals, 46 million apart, unexplained by either source.
- The **precedents table** used diesel prices and year-on-year changes from the data file that mix reference weeks (for example March 2022: +51.6% in the file, +50.0% on the same MASE week a year earlier; May 2026 used the week before the protest). The script now recomputes them from the MASE weekly series, with the pre-2022 weeks read from the MASE CSV and stored in `EXTERNAL`.

Method: every number was recomputed with Python from `docs/data/*.json`; 27 links in the report were downloaded (22 readable, 5 blocked: gasworld and iea.org outside the network allow-list, CNR ×2 with 403, Sky TG24 error page); the MASE weekly CSV (`sisen.mase.gov.it/dgsaie/api/v1/weekly-prices/report/export?format=CSV`) was downloaded and matches `italia-impatti.json` to the fourth decimal for every week compared; Yahoo Finance daily and hourly bars were read for BZ=F, TTF=F and EURUSD=X; blocked pages were checked through web search (gasworld, IEA, art. 24-ter, Istat).

Outcomes: **ok** = matches; **corrected** = wrong or imprecise, fixed in the script; **n.v.** = not verifiable from here.

## 2. Scenarios, backtest and the excise-refund argument

- **Scenario table:** all 8 rows match `italia-impatti.json` `scenari` (diesel, petrol, PUN, regulated gas, inflation, stoppage risk). The ranges are labelled *Assessment*. ok.
- **Method:** the TransMed input is 20.86 bcm (Mazara's 12-month flow, `gas-italia.json`), net of 7.9 bcm of spare regasification capacity at the low end, no bypass at the high end. The text said only "net of spare capacity": corrected.
- **Base prices:** pre-war Brent 71.27 is the 23–27 February weekly average (Yahoo daily closes average 71.27); the "today" base 91.70 is the overnight price described above. Stated in the Method paragraph and in Limits.
- **Backtest, 1 month:** rule 1.96–2.21; observed (4 weeks to 1 April: 9, 16, 23, 30 March) average 1.990 and peak 2.033 (16 March) with the cuts; 2.112 and 2.277 without them (+0.244 on 23 and 30 March). All reproduced. ok.
- **Backtest, 3 months:** rule 2.03–2.28; without cuts average 2.221, peak 2.397 on 13 April (2.1534 + 0.244). The average is inside the range, the peak above it. ok.
- **Inflation:** 1.5 (Feb) → 1.7 (Mar) → 2.7 (Apr) → 3.0 (Jun); +1.2 and +1.5 points against a direct effect of +1.4–2.3 and +1.4–2.5. March added to the text, since the 1-month window ends on 1 April. ok.
- **PUN:** rule 156–174 vs March 143.4. ok. **Red Sea:** 1.754 in the week of 11 December 2023, 1.728 average over the next 4 weeks. ok.
- **Excise cuts took 12–19 cents off the average diesel price:** 2.112 − 1.990 = 12.2; 2.221 − 2.033 = 18.8. ok.
- **Excise refund mechanism (checked against the law):** art. 24-ter of the excise code refunds to hauliers (trucks ≥ 7.5 t, Euro V+) the excise paid above the reference rate of €403.22 per 1,000 litres. At the ordinary €672.90 the refund is 26.97 c/l (Federtrasporti says 26.5). A general cut of 20 c (2026) brings the excise to €472.90 and the refund to 6.97 c: the haulier's net excise stays at 40.32 c. The author's argument is therefore right, and stronger than written: the cut is worth nothing in final cost to an eligible truck (VAT is recovered anyway), only cash flow, as long as it is under ~27 c. Unatras's April demand of 200 euros per 1,000 litres to compensate the "lost refund" matches the 20-cent cut exactly. The cost calculation is corrected accordingly: because the eligible truck's excise is fixed, the percentage rise in its fuel cost is larger (+43%), not smaller.
- **Assessments marked:** every paragraph of reasoning carries *Assessment* (box in the HTML); the new sentence on the €2.29 estimate being an upper bound is marked; the key-point causal claims are now either sourced (ministry on the price cap) or labelled calculation/assessment.

## 3. Conflicts the author listed: resolution

| Conflict | Resolution |
|---|---|
| Brent 91.70 vs 92.62 | Neither is the close. 91.70 (prezzi.json, read 03:40 UTC on 10 Nov) is overnight trading of the 10 November session; 92.62 is an intraday reading at 19:47 UTC on 9 Nov; the 9 November close is **92.57** (Yahoo, read 06:49 UTC on 10 Nov). The report quotes 92.57 and explains the other two; the scenarios keep 91.70 (impact < 0.5 c on diesel). `prezzi.json` still flags 91.70 as provisional. **Recommendation for the data owner:** the collector should not take the last bar of a futures contract read after 18:00 New York time as the previous session's close. The risk dashboard and the Hormuz report (92.62, "provisional") are within 0.05 of the close and need no change. |
| Haulage credit 480 vs 434 million | Both are allocations (MIT 9 Nov: 480 allocated, 242.2 granted; Unatras 21 Oct: 434 allocated, not yet received). The difference (46 m) is unexplained; stated. The earlier text ("434 million not yet paid") was a misreading. |
| June 2026 emergency stocks | 89.7 days between 76.6 and 77.3: a one-month spike, almost certainly a reporting or revision artefact in Eurostat; it is not used in any calculation and the report says so. |
| Regression 2021–2026 vs data from January 2022 | The coefficients were estimated by the collector on 304 MASE weeks from 11 January 2021; the file keeps 253 weeks from January 2022, so they cannot be re-estimated from the repository alone. The MASE CSV (checked) has the missing weeks. Stated in Limits. |
| French CNR diesel weight | Not verifiable from here (PDF 403); the vehicle is a long-haul articulated truck (the "40-tonne" detail removed). Kept as an approximation, reliability medium, marked not verified. |
| La Spezia's Qatar LNG dependency | A rule, not a flow: `port-risk.json` gives every Italian LNG port a primary dependency on Qatar LNG because Italy's national Comtrade share from the Gulf is 32.6%. The text now says so and explains that the score falls mainly if the Qatar LNG and Red Sea dashboard scores fall. |
